An [[obsidian]]-[[Color|black]]-plated<ref name="Chapter 22 AD" /> '''RA-7 protocol droid''' once worked for the [[Galactic Empire]]. After [[Battle of Jakku|fall of the Galactic Empire]], the [[droid]] was reprogrammed to serve the [[Royal family of Plazir-15|Royal family]] of the independent [[planet]] [[Plazir-15]].<ref name="Chapter 22" /> In [[9 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{MandoDate|22}}</ref> the RA-7 waited together with a similarly black-plated [[R-series]] [[astromech droid]] on a docking platform outside the [[Unidentified domed city|domed city]] where the Royal family resided as [[Bo-Katan Kryze's Gauntlet starfighter|a Gauntlet starfighter]] descended. The RA-7 then greeted the exiting [[Mandalorian]]s [[Din Djarin]], [[Bo-Katan Kryze]], and [[Din Grogu|Grogu]] and told them to proceed to their assigned [[hyperloop pod]] waiting for them. After the two droids were out of listening reach, Djarin whispered to Kryze and asked her why there were Imperial droids on an independent world and Kryze replied that she didn't knew either.<ref name="Chapter 22" />

{{Char-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
The RA-7 protocol droid first appeared in "[[Chapter 22: Guns for Hire]]" the sixth episode of the [[The Mandalorian Season Three|third season]] of the live-action television series ''[[Star Wars: The Mandalorian]]'', which was directed by [[Bryce Dallas Howard]]<ref name="Chapter 22" /> and released on [[April 5]], [[2023]].<ref name="Writers Guild">{{WebCite|url=https://directories.wga.org/project/1185542/the-mandalorian|text=The Mandalorian|work=[https://www.wga.org wga.org]|archivedate=20221204123657}}</ref> The droid was physically portrayed by [[Chris Bartlett]] and simply credited as "RA-7 Performance Artist".<ref name="Chapter 22" /> The audio description on [[Disney+]] describes the RA-7 as "a black [[Death Star]] model [[protocol droid]]".<ref name="Chapter 22 AD" />
